title: C++20 CPU Machine Learning Library
meta: C++20 · Apple Silicon · CPU kernels · end-to-end training
summary: From-scratch CPU deep-learning stack with a float32 tensor core, custom kernels, and end-to-end MNIST training.
context: I built this to understand modern training systems from first principles: math kernels, memory layout, backward passes, and reproducible benchmarking.
architecture: Implemented MLP, CNN, and RNN modules with explicit forward/backward paths and reusable module APIs.
Shipped a dual-path f32 GEMM backend: BLAS for large matrix multiplies and custom blocked ARM NEON micro-kernels for tuned hot paths.
Built convolution as im2col-to-GEMM with parallel im2col/col2im and cached patch buffers for faster backward weight updates.
outcomes: Reached ~96% MNIST test accuracy in ~19s for 10 epochs on Apple Silicon (batch size 128).
Added 13 CTest suites, finite-difference gradient checks, GEMM reference equivalence tests, and benchmark smoke coverage in CI.
Produced per-epoch CSV metrics and standalone HTML dashboards for training analysis.

title: GEMM Kernel
meta: C++20 · ARM NEON · cache blocking · multithreading
summary: Progressive optimization of matrix multiplication on Apple M2 from naive loops to packed, SIMD, multi-threaded kernels.
context: This project is a full optimization journey: each version isolates one idea (loop order, blocking, vectorization, packing, threading) and measures its impact.
architecture: Built v0→v6 kernel progression: naive, loop-reordered, blocked, scalar tiled, NEON micro-kernels, packed layout, and parallel execution.
Designed atlas_memory workspace primitives for aligned packed buffers and predictable memory access.
Integrated correctness tests against reference implementations and OpenBLAS comparison tests.
outcomes: Measured up to 270.55 GFLOP/s on 1024^3 workloads on Apple M2.
Recorded a 200x speedup over naive baseline and outperformed tuned 8-thread OpenBLAS in local benchmark scenarios.
Documented architecture notes, blocking strategy, micro-kernel design, and profiling workflow.

title: 3D Audio
meta: C++17 · miniaudio · GLFW · OpenGL · Dear ImGui
summary: Interactive desktop spatial-audio workstation that simulates direction, depth, and height cues over stereo playback.
context: The focus was perceptual realism under real-time callback constraints: useful audio cues, low latency, and a UI that stays in sync with DSP state.
architecture: Implemented VBAP panning, Woodworth-style interaural time delays, rear-source filtering, and distance-aware attenuation.
Built a callback-driven 48 kHz float-stereo engine with fractional delay lines, three-band crossovers, and smoothed runtime parameters.
Added an OpenGL/ImGui editor for drag-and-drop source placement and listener orientation, synchronized with the audio thread.
outcomes: Delivered click-free interactive control with parameter smoothing designed for live manipulation.
Simulated early room reflections (floor/ceiling paths) to improve height and space perception.
Shipped presets and direct coordinate controls for fast audition and repeatable scene setup.

title: Polygraph
summary: Prediction-market graph intelligence system that ingests public market data, infers typed edges, and serves an interactive explorer.
context: I wanted a practical way to reason about market structure beyond isolated charts, with explicit provenance for every inferred relationship.
architecture: Ingested ~45k markets/events/tags from public APIs into SQLite and built local FTS5 + vector retrieval.
Implemented a tiered inference pipeline for structural, temporal, semantic, and empirical relationship edges.
Exported GraphML and served an interactive web UI with neighborhood exploration, filtering, and market detail views.
outcomes: Resolved 195k+ typed relationships across 38k+ connected markets with confidence/provenance metadata.
Enabled sub-millisecond keyword + semantic retrieval with an offline-built MiniLM embedding index.
Automated refresh flows (fetch/embed/prices/infer/build) for repeatable updates.

title: Blackjack Engine
meta: C++20 · TypeScript · React · CMake · Apple Accelerate
summary: Casino-grade blackjack simulator with side bets, web terminal UI, and a C++ reinforcement-learning training stack.
context: This project combines deterministic game-engine correctness with practical experimentation: simulation, strategy comparison, and training loops.
architecture: Implemented American blackjack rules (6-deck shoe, hole card, peek, S17, insurance/even money) plus Perfect Pairs and 21+3 side bets.
Built a TypeScript server and React terminal-style frontend for interactive gameplay and settlement tracking.
Added a C++ RL module with MDP environment wrappers, state encoders, policy/value MLPs, and episodic training utilities.
outcomes: Created a reproducible framework to compare random, heuristic, and learned strategies under identical game rules.
Kept engine and training components in a shared codebase to reduce divergence between simulation and learning environments.
Structured the project for both CLI and web workflows.

title: Noisegen
summary: Loopable long-form noise video pipeline with programmatic soundscapes, reactive visuals, and efficient duration scaling.
context: The core idea is to render a short seamless loop once, then scale duration with stream-copy looping so 1-hour and 10-hour outputs have similar render cost.
architecture: Generated stereo noise/soundscape loops (48 kHz) with crossfade-seam closure, voicing controls, and reverb that preserves loop periodicity.
Built a raylib visual renderer with deterministic phase-driven scenes and headless frame output for ffmpeg muxing.
Composed an end-to-end shell pipeline (audio synthesis → visualization → encode → long-duration loop).
outcomes: Supports multiple noise colors and procedural ambience presets (rain, ocean, wind, fire, stream, drone).
Produces long-duration outputs efficiently by looping encoded base clips rather than rerendering full timelines.
Provides both interactive preview and batch rendering workflows.

title: DC-UTPX
meta: C++ · userspace transport · telemetry · congestion control
summary: Userspace UDP transport protocol for data-center incast workloads with ECN-aware control and microburst pacing.
context: Designed for fan-in congestion scenarios where tail latency and fairness collapse under synchronized bursts.
architecture: Combined DCTCP-style ECN feedback with delay/loss signals for congestion control decisions.
Added pacing controls to smooth synchronized sender bursts under incast pressure.
Collected per-flow telemetry for RTT percentiles, congestion window trajectories, and ECN-mark fractions.
outcomes: 99.97% delivery ratio and P99 RTT under 2.2 ms across 73 concurrent flows in stress tests.
Measured 9x aggregate throughput over kernel TCP under synchronized incast (856 Mbps vs 95 Mbps).
Observed Jain fairness index >= 0.945 with goodput loss below 0.003% in tested scenarios.
